cases.title: Record, Edit and Delete Personal Transactions
cases.goal: Maintain income and expense records, optional receipts and correct balances without duplicate posting.
cases.trigger: The user selects Add transaction or opens an owned transaction.
cases.pre:
1. User has an authorized session, or an unlocked encrypted cache after initial sign-in for the offline branch.
2. An owned wallet and applicable category exist.
3. Group records are not edited through this flow.
cases.fr: Income/expense capture, receipts, editing, deletion and offline pending changes.
cases.nfr: NFR-S4, NFR-S6, NFR-S8, NFR-R3, NFR-R5, NFR-R6
cases.input: Enter amount, wallet, category, date and note; optionally attach a receipt.
cases.review: Review a 120,000 VND Food expense and the selected wallet.
cases.commit: Validate ownership and category type; atomically record the transaction and its attachment references; update derived totals.
cases.result: One expense appears in history; Cash decreases by 120,000 VND and Food spending increases once.

a: Step 2: change type or open an existing entry
1. Choose an income category or edit allowed values. 2. Recalculate affected wallet/category totals; keep the original ID when editing.
1. Confirm deletion and recalculate. 2. Offer Undo for 7 seconds; valid Undo restores the same ID/values once. If expired or unavailable, return to history without recreating it.
1. Save an authorized personal change locally as Pending and invoke UC-DL-12 on reconnection. 2. If only the receipt fails after posting, retry the upload without another financial entry.
Local and server status remain distinct.
Step 2: money relates to a group event
1. Select the authorized source event. 2. Link the movement rather than creating another consumption entry; the user's share is counted once.
Cash and consumption are not duplicated.
Step 3: bad amount/date/category/receipt or ineligible wallet
1. Identify the invalid field/file or reference. 2. Retain valid input and ask for correction; reject the whole invalid write.

cases.title: Record and Confirm Shared-Fund Contributions
cases.support: Group Owner acting as fund custodian.
cases.goal: Record money contributed outside the app and increase the shared fund only after the custodian confirms receipt.
cases.trigger: A member opens the group fund and selects Contribute.
cases.pre:
1. Both actors have online authorized group sessions.
2. The group fund exists and is active.
3. Actual payment occurs outside FinSync.
cases.fr: Contribution claims, custodian confirmation, fund and member-position visibility.
cases.input: Enter the amount/date and declare that the external contribution was made.
cases.review: Review a 500,000 VND contribution claim; explain that it does not increase the fund yet.
cases.commit: Save a pending claim; notify the Owner; the Owner opens it, verifies receipt and confirms; atomically post the fund credit.
cases.result: Fund balance becomes 1,500,000 VND; Laura's confirmed contribution position increases by 500,000; no expense is created.

a: Step 4: no confirmation, rejection or contributor withdrawal

Step 4: another member confirms or status already changed
1. Require the fund custodian. 2. Recheck claim status; a prior confirmation returns its existing result, a conflicting decision is rejected.
1. Show confirmed cash and member positions separately from pending claims. 2. Show zero if empty; unused-fund return opens UC-DL-08.

cases.title: Record and Split a Group Expense
cases.support: Group Owner when authorizing shared-fund spending.
cases.goal: Allocate a real group expense exactly, preserve the funding source and update member positions without counting consumption twice.
cases.trigger: An authorized member selects Add group expense.
cases.pre:
1. Online active membership.
2. Group currency and participants are known.
3. A valid rate exists for a foreign-currency bill; sufficient fund cash exists for fund-funded spending.
cases.fr: Single-payer/fund-funded expense, equal/exact/percentage/weighted allocation and exact rounding.
cases.input: Enter title/date/category, payer or fund, original amount/currency and participating members; select split mode.
cases.review: Review You 100,001; Laura 100,000; Minh 100,000 VND. Total equals 300,001 VND.
cases.commit: Revalidate membership, quote, split inputs and funding; atomically post the expense, allocations and the applicable payer/fund entry.
cases.result: One expense appears. Member debt/fund positions update; each user's consumption is only their allocated share.

a: 1. Enter exact amounts totaling the bill, percentages totaling 100%, or positive weights. 2. Calculate final shares and distribute rounding remainders in a stable order.
Final shares sum exactly to the expense.
1. Verify all selected identities belong to the group. 2. Recalculate and remove obsolete draft allocations before review.
No hidden shares for removed participants.
1. Check custodian permission and available confirmed cash. 2. Debit the fund instead of crediting an individual payer; update member fund positions once.
Only one funding source is used.
1. Show original amount and rate/source/time. 2. Convert once, then split and retain the snapshot. Missing/changed quote requires a new review.
No silent repricing of historical shares.
Step 3 or 4: mismatch, no participants, bad weights or low fund cash
1. Display the difference or available amount. 2. Keep the draft and reject the entire expense until corrected.
No partial expense, allocation or fund debit.

cases.title: View Debts and Confirm a Settlement
cases.goal: Inspect simplified debts and reduce debt only after the intended recipient confirms an external payment.
cases.trigger: The user opens Who owes whom and selects a debt.
cases.pre:
1. Both parties are authorized active group members online.
2. A positive outstanding debt exists.
3. The debtor pays outside FinSync before claiming payment.
cases.fr: Net debt summary, simplified suggestions, payment claims, partial settlement and recipient confirmation.
cases.input: Select the intended recipient, amount and date; indicate that external payment has occurred.
cases.review: Review the payer, recipient and claim amount; display Awaiting recipient confirmation.
cases.commit: Create a pending claim; notify the recipient; recipient confirms receipt after current-debt validation; atomically post settlement effects.
cases.result: Confirmed debt falls from 100,000 to 0 VND. The payment remains in history and is not new spending.

a: 1. Show transfers preserving every member's net position. 2. If requested, send an eligible deduplicated reminder; do not create a payment.
Step 2: amount is below outstanding debt
1. Review the smaller positive amount. 2. After recipient confirmation reduce only that amount: 50,000 paid against 100,000 leaves 50,000.
Step 4: recipient does not confirm, rejects, or debtor cancels
1. Keep pending debt unchanged. 2. Record rejection reason or cancel an unconfirmed claim; never cancel an already confirmed payment through this branch.
Step 4: Owner or another person tries to confirm
1. Check intended recipient identity. 2. Reject confirmation by anyone else, including the Owner.
Step 3 or 4: invalid/excess amount or changed debt
1. Recompute current outstanding debt. 2. Reject an excess claim and request fresh review; repeated confirmation returns the existing result.

cases.title: Record Expense Refunds and Return Unused Funds
cases.actor: Group Member who recorded the expense / authorized Group Owner
cases.support: Intended recipient for an unused-fund return.
cases.goal: Record traceable corrections and reimbursements without deleting settled financial history.
cases.trigger: The user opens an original group expense and selects Record refund, or opens Return unused funds.
cases.pre:
1. Online authorized membership.
2. Original confirmed expense exists for expense refunds.
3. Remaining refundable amount and original participants/rate are available.
cases.fr: Linked partial/full refunds, exact reversal, post-settlement reimbursement and confirmed fund returns.
cases.input: Select the original expense; enter refund amount/date/reason and actual recipient of the external refund.
cases.review: Review a 90,000 VND refund: reverse 30,000 consumption per original participant.
cases.commit: Validate remaining refundable amount; atomically append a linked adjustment using original allocations and stored currency basis; retain all earlier payments.
cases.result: Net consumption is 210,000 VND. If already settled, reimbursement positions appear; no prior settlement is deleted.

a: 1. Show unrefunded expense and per-member amounts. 2. Reverse only the selected remaining amount using the original allocation/rate basis and exact rounding.
Cumulative refunds never exceed original shares.
Step 4: original debt was already paid
1. Retain all prior payments. 2. Show new reimbursement positions; any subsequent external payment uses UC-DL-07.
1. Verify the original funding source and returned money. 2. Credit the fund and reverse allocated consumption once.
1. Check cash and the member's entitlement; create a return claim. 2. Intended recipient confirms receipt; pending/rejected/withdrawn claims do not reduce confirmed cash.
Confirmed return reduces cash and entitlement once.
Step 3 or 4: missing original, excess amount, missing quote or stale entitlement
1. Show the current permitted amount or missing evidence. 2. Reject the adjustment and retain a correctable draft; the Owner cannot confirm receipt for another member.

cases.title: Synchronize Offline Personal Changes and Resolve Conflicts
cases.support: None; connectivity detection and synchronization worker are internal.
cases.goal: Submit encrypted locally queued personal changes exactly once and explicitly resolve version conflicts.
cases.trigger: Connectivity returns or the user selects Sync now after offline capture.
cases.pre:
1. Initial authenticated synchronization has created an account-specific encrypted cache.
2. Stable operation IDs, base versions and pending changes exist.
3. Valid online session is available for server submission.
cases.fr: Offline personal CRUD, durable pending queue, idempotent reconciliation, conflict resolution and receipt retry.
cases.input: Unlock the local account cache, inspect pending records and select Sync now.
cases.review: Show pending operation IDs/order and local-only labels; verify session before submission.
cases.commit: Submit operations with stable IDs/base versions; validate on server; acknowledge committed results; mark only acknowledged operations synchronized.
cases.result: Three changes synchronize once; local IDs match server records; balances refresh and pending status clears.

a: 1. Keep unacknowledged operations durable. 2. Resume remaining work on reconnection; already acknowledged items stay synchronized.
No acknowledged local edit is lost.
Step 3: authorization unavailable or logout requested
1. Pause and request valid sign-in for the same account. 2. Before logout warn about pending edits; allow cancel-and-sync or explicit discard, then clear account-local data.
1. Show local/server values and any tombstone. 2. Keep server, reapply against the refreshed version, or explicitly recreate a deleted entry with a new ID; never overwrite/resurrect silently.
1. Reuse the original operation identity and retrieve its outcome. 2. Acknowledge the existing result without applying it again.
Step 4: wallet/category ineligible or upload fails
1. Mark the invalid operation Action required and retain its draft; retry only a failed receipt upload. 2. Continue independent valid records.
No second financial entry; partial progress is explicit.
Step 2: user tries to change shared data
1. Show cached group data as read-only. 2. Require an online session before shared writes; do not enqueue them as personal changes.

cases.title: Generate Financial Reports on Demand or Automatically
cases.actor: Regular User; Deployment Scheduler for monthly runs
cases.support: Authorized operator monitoring or retrying a scheduled run.
cases.goal: Produce authorized personal/group reports with consistent totals, an explicit currency basis and optional PDF/Excel output.
cases.trigger: The user opens Reports, or the monthly scheduler starts a due report.
cases.pre:
1. Valid user or scheduler authorization.
2. Requested data scope and period are permitted.
3. Conversion-dependent totals have an identified rate basis.
cases.fr: On-demand and monthly report aggregation, filters, private publication and PDF/Excel export.
cases.nfr: NFR-S4, NFR-R3, NFR-R8; DL-NFR-02 and DL-NFR-03 below.
cases.input: Choose personal/group scope, period, currency and output format; a scheduled run derives the closed month for each eligible user.
cases.review: Review the period, currency basis and source cutoff; preview the same totals used for details and export.
cases.commit: Aggregate the authorized snapshot; generate the report and requested artifact; record completion before publication.
cases.result: The user can inspect or download the report with period/currency/cutoff labels. A scheduled result is published once; the financial ledger is unchanged.

a: Step 1: scheduled trigger instead of user request
1. Select each eligible user's closed month/currency. 2. Generate and publish one authorized result; duplicate triggers reuse the same logical run.
1. Recheck group access and apply the same filters to totals and details. 2. Export the reviewed snapshot as PDF or Excel; never expose private member wallets.
Empty data / invalid range / missing rate
Step 3: unavailable or invalid reporting inputs
1. Reject invalid ranges; show zero/empty data or growth as not applicable for a zero baseline. 2. If conversion is missing, show original-currency subtotals and incomplete status.
Step 3 or 5: offline viewing or source changes
1. Label cached/pending data and its cutoff. 2. Regeneration creates an explicit revised snapshot; it does not silently rewrite a previously issued report.
The report remains attributable to its source period.
Step 4 or 5: an output stage fails
1. Preserve confirmed results and retry the failed unit without re-posting financial data. 2. Keep delivery pending, or mark failed after the retry limit; revoke access if eligibility changed.
No false success or unauthorized download.
Step 4: worker restart or operator stop
1. Resume from acknowledged work without duplicating published results, or stop new work at safe boundaries. 2. Retain completed results and expose remaining/failed counts.

cases.title: Evaluate Budget Alerts and Send Debt Reminders in Batches
cases.support: Regular User receiving alerts; authorized operator retrying failed items.
cases.goal: Evaluate many eligible budgets/debts reliably and deliver each logical alert once without changing recorded balances.
cases.trigger: A scheduled sweep starts or an authorized operator resumes failed notification work.
cases.pre:
1. Valid scheduler identity and configured recipient-local schedule.
2. Budget/debt data is available.
3. Durable checkpoints, deduplication keys and delivery state are available.
cases.fr: Bounded batch processing, exact threshold/debt evaluation, retry/recovery, notification deduplication and operational audit.
cases.nfr: NFR-S4, NFR-R3, NFR-U6; DL-NFR-02 and DL-NFR-03 below.
cases.input: Authenticate the trigger; select eligible users and a stable sweep window; create or reuse the run.
cases.review: Claim a bounded page with a lease; expose processed/failed counts and the checkpoint, not private transaction details.
cases.commit: Recompute current consumption and confirmed debts; atomically insert eligible deduplicated inbox/outbox events and acknowledge the item; advance the checkpoint only after commit.
cases.result: Eligible users receive one logical threshold/reminder event; completed items are counted; financial balances remain unchanged.

a: Step 2 or 4: no eligible event or existing logical alert
1. Skip the item or finish with zero recipients. 2. Do not create placeholder or duplicate messages.
Step 4 or 5: queued information became stale
1. Recheck debt and recipient rights. 2. Suppress obsolete reminders or protected content before delivery.
No false debt reminder or data leak.
Step 3 or 4: concurrent processing or worker failure
1. Resume unacknowledged work only. 2. Reject stale completion and reuse existing committed event identities.
No lost acknowledged item or duplicate event.
Step 4 or 5: evaluation or delivery fails
1. Retry transient errors within a configured limit; retain the failed item after permanent/exhausted failure. 2. Continue other recipients and report Partial/Failed.
Failure is visible and retryable, not silently dropped.
Step 1 or 3: invalid service identity or operator stop
1. Reject an invalid/untracked start, or stop new claims at item boundaries. 2. Keep completed events and checkpoints for an authorized resume.
No uncontrolled processing or ledger change.
